```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
options(HTTPUserAgent = "3MB001-course", timeout = 60)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE)
use_snapshot <- FALSE
snapshot_date <- "2026-11-18"
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
provenance <- data.frame(dataset = character(), mode = character(),
                         retrieved = character(), version = character())

# Daily cache includes provenance. Failures use the named snapshot, never
# unlabelled made-up data. Missing or malformed snapshots stop the report.
load_data <- function(name, snapshot, fetch_fun, snapshot_version,
                      snapshot_read = function(path) {
                        read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                                 na.strings = character())
                      }) {
  cache <- file.path("data", paste0(name, "-", Sys.Date(), ".rds"))
  if (use_snapshot) {
    obj <- list(data = snapshot_read(snapshot), mode = "course snapshot",
                retrieved = snapshot_date, version = snapshot_version)
  } else if (file.exists(cache)) {
    obj <- readRDS(cache)
    obj$mode <- paste("cached", obj$mode)
  } else {
    obj <- tryCatch({
      value <- fetch_fun()
      version <- attr(value, "source_version")
      if (is.null(version)) version <- "not reported"
      result <- list(data = value, mode = "live API", retrieved = as.character(Sys.Date()),
                     version = version)
      saveRDS(result, cache)
      result
    }, error = function(e) {
      warning(paste("API unavailable:", conditionMessage(e), "Using course snapshot."))
      list(data = snapshot_read(snapshot), mode = "fallback snapshot",
           retrieved = snapshot_date, version = snapshot_version)
    })
  }
  provenance <<- rbind(provenance, data.frame(dataset = name, mode = obj$mode,
                         retrieved = obj$retrieved, version = obj$version))
  obj$data
}
uniprot_release <- function(url) {
  headers <- tryCatch(curlGetHeaders(url), error = function(e) character())
  h <- headers[grepl("^x-uniprot-release:", headers, ignore.case = TRUE)]
  if (length(h)) trimws(sub("^[^:]+:", "", tail(h, 1))) else "not reported"
}
count_feature <- function(x, token) {
  vapply(gregexpr(token, x, fixed = TRUE), function(pos) sum(pos > 0), integer(1))
}
```

# Data: fifteen human proteins

The labels below group teaching examples by their main role in these lectures;
proteins can have additional locations. PEX5 is an import **receptor**, not a
peroxisomal matrix cargo. The report is not a universal location predictor.

```{r proteins-and-query}
markers <- data.frame(
  accession = c("P02768", "P01308", "P11021", "P27824", "P07237", "P11279",
                "P04062", "P01130", "P02786", "Q8NBP7", "P25705", "O75390",
                "P37198", "P50542", "P04406"),
  destination = c("Secreted", "Secreted", "ER", "ER", "ER", "Lysosome",
                  "Lysosome", "Cell surface", "Cell surface", "Secreted",
                  "Mitochondrion", "Mitochondrion", "Nuclear pore",
                  "Peroxisome import receptor", "Cytosol"))
query_base <- paste0("https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/accessions?accessions=",
                      paste(markers$accession, collapse = ","))
uniprot_url <- paste0(query_base,
  "&fields=accession,gene_primary,ft_signal,ft_transit,ft_transmem,cc_subcellular_location,sequence&format=tsv")
fasta_url <- paste0(query_base, "&format=fasta")
fetch_features <- function() {
  x <- read.delim(uniprot_url, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                  na.strings = character(), quote = "")
  stopifnot(setequal(x$Entry, markers$accession))
  attr(x, "source_version") <- uniprot_release(uniprot_url)
  x
}
raw_features <- load_data("uniprot-features", "data/uniprot-features-2026-11-18.csv",
                          fetch_features, "UniProtKB 2026_04")
expected_columns <- c("Entry", "Gene Names (primary)", "Signal peptide",
                      "Transit peptide", "Transmembrane", "Subcellular location [CC]",
                      "Sequence")
stopifnot(setequal(raw_features$Entry, markers$accession),
          identical(names(raw_features), expected_columns))
proteins <- raw_features
names(proteins) <- c("accession", "gene", "signal", "transit", "transmembrane",
                     "location", "sequence")
proteins$destination <- markers$destination[match(proteins$accession, markers$accession)]
head(proteins[c("accession", "gene", "destination")])
```

## Read FASTA and align by accession

Each header starts `>sp|ACCESSION|ENTRY_NAME`. One sequence can span several lines.
This helper handles those line breaks and rejects duplicated accessions.

```{r fasta-helper}
parse_fasta <- function(lines) {
  starts <- which(startsWith(lines, ">"))
  stopifnot(length(starts) > 0, starts[1] == 1)
  ends <- c(starts[-1] - 1, length(lines))
  accession <- vapply(strsplit(sub("^>", "", lines[starts]), "|", fixed = TRUE),
                       function(x) x[2], character(1))
  sequence <- vapply(seq_along(starts), function(i) {
    if (ends[i] <= starts[i]) stop("FASTA header without sequence")
    paste0(trimws(lines[seq.int(starts[i] + 1, ends[i])]), collapse = "")
  }, character(1))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(accession), all(nchar(sequence) > 0))
  data.frame(accession = accession, sequence = sequence)
}
fetch_fasta <- function() {
  lines <- readLines(fasta_url, warn = FALSE)
  stopifnot(length(lines) > 0, startsWith(lines[1], ">"))
  attr(lines, "source_version") <- uniprot_release(fasta_url)
  lines
}
fasta_lines <- load_data("uniprot-fasta", "data/uniprot-sequences-2026-11-18.fasta",
                         fetch_fasta, "UniProtKB 2026_04",
                         snapshot_read = function(path) readLines(path, warn = FALSE))
fasta <- parse_fasta(fasta_lines)
stopifnot(setequal(fasta$accession, proteins$accession))
fasta_sequence <- fasta$sequence[match(proteins$accession, fasta$accession)]
# Do not compare rows until the records have been aligned by accession.
stopifnot(identical(fasta_sequence, proteins$sequence))
```

feature annotations and FASTA sequences must refer to the same protein set.
